outcome.technical: _proc_group.py: split tear_down into _kill (seam; kill command success only: killpg+wait on POSIX, taskkill exit 0 on Windows) and _gone (proc.poll() reaps, then _locks.pid_alive(pid) is False; alive or unaskable = not gone). tear_down returns bool(killed) or _gone(proc), so a failed kill (taskkill not found, killpg on ended group) is confirmed when the root is gone and unconfirmed when alive. The shares-our-group narrow-kill arm is unchanged (still False) but skipped when the child is already gone. _proc_group now imports _locks, so _deps.LAYERS moves _proc_group from the _locks layer into the layer above (the _panel_ui tuple) with comment updated; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md module-map line now reads '_proc_group -> _locks, _output' (from _deps.py --render). Tests added in test_run_test_gate.py after lc10b: lc10c (kill stubbed to fail, child already exited -> True) and lc10d (kill stubbed to fail, child alive -> False and still running). Callers derive-phase-gate and stamp-verification needed no change; their suites pass. run-test-gate.py and test__proc_group.py unchanged.
outcome.descriptive: A timed-out step's teardown is confirmed by the root process being gone, not by the kill command's exit code, closing the timing-dependent lc10b failure on Windows.
